info.title: App AI Gateway API v2
info.description: A provider-native AI proxy for iOS applications and trusted server backends. Provider keys stay on the gateway; requests are checked, limited and recorded before they reach a provider.

servers.description: The cloud API host. On a self-hosted gateway, use your own origin.

tags.name: App sign-in
tags.description: App Attest challenges and keys, and exchanging a client proof for a gateway token.

tags.name: Admin providers
tags.description: Provider connections and their keys. A key is write-only: only its hint is ever returned.

GatewayBearer.description: A gateway access token from POST /v2/apps/{app}/auth/token, or an app key for a server app that signs no users in. On App Attest apps that sign every request, the request also carries X-AppAttest-Proof.

ManagementBearer.description: A management key. It acts for one account, with the read or manage grant it was issued with. Writes need the manage grant and an owner or admin role.

accepts_app_transaction.description: True when the token exchange accepts app_transaction. A client sends one, and signs over its hash, only when this says so.

data.description: Machine-readable facts about this refusal, present only where the code alone is not actionable. A rate_limited refusal carries scope, limit, windowSeconds, retryAfterSeconds and resetAt.

recorded.description: False when the challenge was never issued for this app, or was already spent or reported.

step.description: The step that failed after the challenge was issued: attest_key, generate_assertion, issuer_token, register or token.

domain.description: The error's domain, such as com.apple.devicecheck.error. Stored only when it is a short token (letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, at most 64 characters); anything else is stored as other.

The error's domain, such as com.apple.devicecheck.error. Stored only when it is a short token (letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, at most 64 characters); anything else is stored as other.

recovered.description: True when the app recovered by itself, such as by registering a new key. Recorded as client_recovered.

verify_on.description: On App Attest apps: every_request means every request sent with this token must carry X-AppAttest-Proof; token_exchange means requests carry only the token. Absent on other apps.

app_transaction.description: The App Store's signed AppTransaction (its JWS), which names the Apple Account the install belongs to. When present, the assertion signs client data that also carries app_transaction: the unpadded base64url SHA-256 of this string. One that does not verify names no account, and the install is counted on its own.

install_id.description: The App Attest key id of the install making the request, on App Attest apps. Null on server apps.

requests_today.description: Requests made so far in the current UTC day: by this install on an App Attest app, by this user on a server app. Null when the app sets no per-user limit, in which case requests are not counted.

requests_remaining.description: What is left of requests_per_day. Null when no daily limit is set.

requests_per_minute.description: The per-minute limit on each install (App Attest) or user (server). Null means unlimited.

requests_per_day.description: The per-day limit on each install (App Attest) or user (server). Null means unlimited.

monthly_cost_usd.description: Spent so far in the current UTC month against the budget below, by whoever budget_scope names.

monthly_budget_usd.description: The monthly budget on each Apple Account, install or user. Null means unlimited.

budget_scope.description: Whose month monthly_cost_usd is: apple_account, install or user.

blocked.description: Whether this user has been blocked in the console.

jwks_url.description: An https URL. Stored in the canonical form `URL` prints.
An https URL. Stored in the canonical form `URL` prints.

providers.description: Every provider connection the app's routing names. A disabled one is listed as disabled, and one that was deleted as missing, with a null id.

ready.description: Whether the app is active and at least one connection it names is active.

limitations.description: What this check did not exercise, one sentence each.

installs.description: How many App Attest keys the user holds: one per install. Always 0 on server apps.

is_install.description: Whether this id is itself an App Attest key, so the row is one install.

is_virtual.description: True for a user id that only the app's usage or refusals name, such as a server app's end-user header. Such a user has no row, and cannot be blocked.

charges.description: Charges in the month, corrections not counted.

failed.description: Of those, attempts that did not end with success.

cost_nano.description: What the month cost, in nano-dollars, corrections included.

usage.description: The user's usage in `month`, from the ledger.

reason.description: Why the key was not confirmed. no_probe: this provider has no cheap call to test with. unreachable: no answer in time. unexpected_status: an answer that proves nothing either way. rejected: the provider refused the key.

status.description: The provider's HTTP status, for unexpected_status and rejected.

post.description: Sent by the app when a step after the challenge failed on the device, so the app's auth events can say why. Diagnostic only. It must name a challenge this app issued that nothing has used yet, and uses it up, so one challenge carries at most one report.

post.summary: Exchange a client proof for a gateway token
post.description: App Attest clients send key_id, assertion and challenge; the answer's verify_on says whether requests sent with the token must also carry X-AppAttest-Proof. Server apps with an issuer send api_key and issuer_token. The verified issuer claim is always the user.

post.description: Send `name`, `config` and an optional `status`. The gateway assigns the id: the name made URL-safe plus a random suffix. Every provider connection, operation and model the config names is checked, and a model with no price is refused with `pricing_not_configured`. An app-key app gets its first key, shown once as `api_key`.

patch.description: Applies `operations` in order to the app as `getApp` answers it, then saves the result exactly as `PUT` would: the same checks, the same errors, and nothing written unless every operation applies and the result is accepted. Each operation is RFC 6902 `add`, `replace` or `remove` at a JSON Pointer under `/name`, `/status` or `/config`, for example `{"op": "replace", "path": "/config/limits/per_app/requests/per_minute", "value": 600}`. A value is written as given: `null` sets a limit to unlimited, and only `remove` deletes. Needs `revision`, as `PUT` does. An operation that cannot apply answers `400 invalid_request` naming its index.

post.summary: Check an edit of an app without saving it
post.description: Judged as an update of this app would be. After a provider connection is deleted, an edit may keep that connection's routing entry only if the entry is unchanged; an added or changed entry for it is refused. Needs only the read grant: nothing is saved.

get.summary: Check whether an app is ready to serve requests
get.description: Checks the stored config as an update would, lists every provider connection its routing names with its status (a disabled one as disabled, a deleted one as missing), and answers `ready` when the app is active and at least one of them is active. It sends no provider request, and `limitations` says what it did not try. A stored config that would no longer be accepted answers `400` with the reason.

200.description: What the check found, and what it did not try.

put.description: Needs `revision`. A new non-null `baseUrl` needs `secret` in the same request: a stored key is never sent to a new origin. `baseUrl: null` returns to the provider's own origin. `status: disabled` pauses the connection and keeps its key and slug.
